Live refresh
A table, badge or screen that updates by itself when someone changes a record elsewhere, with no reload. The server sends a list_update message over the socket.
list_update hub
This branch's one listener per doctype (listUpdateHub.ts). Every table and badge set on the page subscribes to it instead of joining the doctype's room on its own.
Data Updated toast
Develop's pop-up note after a table refreshed live. The branch refreshes quietly and shows no toast.
Busy viewer
Someone typing in a table's search, with a row ticked, a dialog open or the pointer on the rows. On the branch a live refresh waits and a 'New changes · Refresh' chip offers it.
Spread
Each table waits 1-2 s and each badge set 2-6 s after a change, picked at random, so many open screens do not all ask the server in the same instant.
Another user
The Administrator, saving through the REST API or a bench console in another session, while the walk's role user watches the screen.
Badge count
A number beside a sidebar entry or a tab (e.g. 'Approve PR'): how many records wait in that state for this user.
Redis table cache

On the branch, a table page (rows for one doctype, page, sort and filters) is kept in Redis for up to 10 s per permission group: users whose list queries get the same permission condition share it, so a second user with the same access gets it without searching the database. Each doctype's version moves on any committed write, which retires its old pages.
R2
The branch's rule that the doctype's cache version moves before the live refresh goes out, so a refresh can never be answered from the old page.
Access scope

What a user may see: an Admin or Accountant sees all; a Project Manager or Procurement Executive only the projects their User Permissions name. Users with a different permission condition never share a kept page.
nc_table_cache
The site config switch for the table cache. Absent or 1: on (the default). 0: off, every page is read from the database.
Room count (#1670)
Develop's count of how many screens hold a doctype's socket room, so closing one screen leaves the room only when no other screen needs it. The branch's hub now shares this count.
